    99→```
   100→
   101→### Agent Workflows
   102→The core logic resides in specialized LangGraph agents. Below is the typical flow for an agent interaction:
   103→
   104→```mermaid
   105→graph TD
   106→    User[User Input] -->|Request Data| ConvAgent[Conversation Agent]
   107→    ConvAgent -->|Generate Response| Guard[Guardrail Agent]
   108→    Guard -->|Validate Content| Decision{Passes<br/>Guardrails?}
   109→    Decision -->|Yes| Tools[Execute Tools/Actions]
   110→    Decision -->|No| Reject[Reject & Request Revision]
   111→    Reject --> ConvAgent
   112→    Tools -->|Tool Results| ConvAgent
   113→    ConvAgent -->|Context Update| Context[(Context Store)]
   114→    Context -->|Enriched Data| ConvAgent
   115→    Guard -->|Approved Response| Output[Deliver to User]
   116→
   117→    classDef agent fill:#d4f1d4,stroke:#28a745,color:#000,stroke-width:2px;
   118→    classDef guard fill:#ffe5cc,stroke:#fd7e14,color:#000,stroke-width:2px;
   119→    classDef decision fill:#e1f5ff,stroke:#007acc,color:#000;
   120→    classDef data fill:#f0f0f0,stroke:#666,color:#000;
   121→
   122→    class ConvAgent agent;
   123→    class Guard guard;
   124→    class Decision decision;
   125→    class Context data;
   126→```
   127→
   128→---
   129→
   130→## 📦 Component Directory
   131→
   132→### Orchestration & Frontend
   133→| Component | Purpose | Path |
   134→| :--- | :--- | :--- |
   135→| **api-service** | Central FastAPI orchestrator. Manages DB persistence and triggers agents. | [api-service](services/api-service/) |
   136→| **hitl-ui** | React/Vite dashboard for human-in-the-loop review and approval. | [hitl-ui](apps/hitl-ui/) |
   137→
   138→### AI Agent Services
   139→| Component | Purpose | Path |
   140→| :--- | :--- | :--- |
   141→| **agent-a-service** | Guest interaction agent using LangGraph flows. | [agent-a-service](services/agent-a-service/) |
   142→| **agent-b-service** | Guardrail agent to validate outputs and ensure safety. | [agent-b-service](services/agent-b-service/) |
   143→
   144→### Data & Infrastructure
   145→| Component | Purpose | Path |
   146→| :--- | :--- | :--- |
   147→| **inference** | Standard AI library for model loading, prompt management (Jinja2), and agent factories. | [inference](libs/inference/) |
   148→| **data-pipeline** | ETL processes for data ingestion, normalization, and prep. | [data-pipeline](libs/data-pipeline/) |
   149→| **evaluation** | Offline benchmarks and metrics for agent performance. | [evaluation](libs/evaluation/) |
   150→| **model-training** | Fine-tuning (LoRA), distillation, and custom model training. | [model-training](libs/model-training/) |
   151→| **shared** | Common Pydantic models and utility functions used by all components. | [shared](libs/shared/) |
   152→
   153→---
   154→
   155→## 🛠️ Key Workflows
   156→
   157→### Creating a New Component
   158→Use the provided script to scaffold a new microservice:
   159→```bash
   160→make create-service
   161→```
   162→
   163→### Database Management
   164→We use **SQLModel** and **Alembic** for schema migrations.
   165→- Create revision: `make db-revision msg="Add table"`
   166→- Apply migration: `make db-migrate`
   167→
   168→### Documentation Site
   169→We use **MkDocs** with the Material theme and `mkdocstrings`.
   170→- Build: `make docs-build`
   171→- Serve: `make docs-serve` (Available at [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000))
   172→
   173→---
   174→
   175→## 🧪 Testing & Quality
   176→
   177→Detailed testing guidelines are available in `docs/testing-guide.md`.
   178→
   179→- **Backend**: `pytest` with 85% coverage threshold (Ruff for linting).
   180→- **Frontend**: `Vitest` for units, `Playwright` for E2E (ESLint for linting).
   181→- **CI/CD**: Configured via GitHub Actions to run tests, linting, and docs building.
   182→
   183→```bash
   184→# Run all tests
   185→make test-python
   186→cd apps/hitl-ui && npm test && npm run test:e2e
   187→
   188→# Run linting
   189→make lint
   190→```
   191→
   192→---
   193→
   194→## 📘 Resources & Further Reading
   195→- [Testing Guide](file:///Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/TemplateRepo_ElixirTrials/docs/testing-guide.md)
   196→- [Local Documentation Index](file:///Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/TemplateRepo_ElixirTrials/docs/index.md)
   197→

     1→# Rune
     2→
     3→## What This Is
     4→
     5→Rune is a local-first coding agent that uses LoRA weight space as episodic memory, enabling unbounded context for Small Language Models (<10B params). Instead of stuffing tokens into context windows, Rune encodes procedural knowledge—architecture specs, execution feedback, coding conventions—directly into composable LoRA adapters via a Doc-to-LoRA hypernetwork. Each coding session produces reusable adapters that persist across sessions and compose hierarchically.
     6→
     7→## Core Value
     8→
     9→A local coding agent that learns from its own coding trajectories, building persistent parametric memory that scales independently of context window size.

    38→- **Hardware target**: Dual RTX 4090 (24GB each, 48GB total VRAM) with CXL interconnect, AMD Threadripper 7960X. Ada Lovelace (sm_89) has mature CUDA/PyTorch/vLLM support. CXL provides cache-coherent memory pooling. QLoRA important for fitting models + adapters in 24GB per GPU.
    39→- **Research basis**: Architecture synthesized from multiple papers (Doc-to-LoRA, S-LoRA, QLoRA, Perceiver, HyperNetworks). No hands-on experiments yet — plan should include early feasibility validation.

    41→- **Base model candidates**: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B (per spec). 24GB per GPU means QLoRA is essential; ~7B models fit comfortably with adapter headroom

    45→- **Local-first**: Must run entirely on local hardware. No cloud API dependencies for inference.

### Executive Summary

Rune's v2.0 milestone is a monorepo restructuring: removing `agent-b-service`, renaming `agent-a-service` to `rune-agent`, creating four new components (`libs/adapter-registry`, `services/lora-server`, `services/training-svc`, `services/evolution-svc`), and extending four existing ones. The work is scaffolding only — typed stubs with `NotImplementedError` bodies and correct workspace wiring, no GPU logic. The uv workspace mechanics are the highest-risk area: a single shared lockfile and five hardcoded path sections in root `pyproject.toml` must be updated in sync.

### Roadmap Implications

Suggested build sequence: 14 steps

1. **Remove agent-b-service** — clean the workspace before adding anything
2. **Rename agent-a → rune-agent** — preserves LangGraph skeleton, safer than create-from-scratch
3. **Scaffold libs/adapter-registry** — dependency root; gate everything else on this
4-7. **Extend existing libs and api-service** — no new workspace members needed
8. **Scaffold lora-server** — Dockerfile-only, NOT a uv workspace member
9-10. **Scaffold training-svc and evolution-svc** — new workspace members
11. **Update rune-agent** — build last; depends on all prior steps
12-14. **Update hitl-ui, docker-compose, mkdocs** — downstream wiring

### Research Flags

Needs research before implementation: Phase 3 (adapter diversity regularization), Phase 4 (hypernetwork architecture choice)
Standard patterns: Scaffold milestone itself (well-documented uv workspace, LangGraph, FastAPI patterns)

### Confidence

Overall: HIGH for scaffold mechanics, MEDIUM for Blackwell ML stack
Key gaps: Dramatiq vs BackgroundTasks at scaffold time; `libs/data-pipeline` and `libs/evaluation` disposition; sandbox strategy for code execution

### Ready for Roadmap

SUMMARY.md written. Roadmapper can proceed to roadmap definition.

    12→Rune's v2.0 milestone is a monorepo restructuring: transforming an ElixirTrials template (with generic agent stubs) into a purpose-built LoRA episodic memory system. The work is primarily scaffolding — creating the correct directory structure, workspace configuration, and typed stubs — not implementing the ML system. The key insight from research is that this milestone should deliver shape, not function: every new component gets proper pyproject.toml wiring, importable stubs with `NotImplementedError` bodies, and clear public interfaces, but no GPU-dependent logic, no business rule implementations, and no integration with external services.
    13→
    14→The restructuring plan is mechanically precise: remove `agent-b-service`, rename `agent-a-service` to `rune-agent`, create four new components (`libs/adapter-registry`, `services/lora-server`, `services/training-svc`, `services/evolution-svc`), and extend four existing ones (`api-service`, `libs/inference`, `libs/model-training`, `libs/shared`). The uv workspace mechanics are the highest-risk area: a single shared lockfile, five hardcoded path sections in root `pyproject.toml`, and mypy override entries must all be updated in sync or CI breaks in silent, hard-to-diagnose ways.
    15→
    16→The dominant engineering constraint beyond scaffolding is Blackwell (RTX 5090, sm_120) compatibility for later implementation phases. This constraint is deferred entirely to training and serving implementation phases — the scaffold milestone runs on CPU and requires no GPU.

   149→| Hypernetwork architecture (`nn.Module` definition) | Phase 4 |
   150→| Tournament selection algorithm | Phase 4 |
   151→| Any real LLM calls, even mocked ones | Phase 3+ |
   152→| MLflow experiment tracking wiring | Phase 2+ |
   153→
   154→---
   155→
   156→## Restructuring Plan
   157→
   158→### Component Mapping: Template → Rune
   159→
   160→| Template Component | Disposition | Result |
   161→|-------------------|-------------|--------|
   162→| `services/agent-a-service` | RENAME | `services/rune-agent` (preserves LangGraph skeleton) |
   163→| `services/agent-b-service` | REMOVE | Deleted; no equivalent in Rune architecture |
   164→| `services/api-service` | EXTEND | Add `/adapters` + `/sessions` routers |
   165→| `libs/shared` | EXTEND | Add `rune_models.py` (`CodingSession`, `AdapterRef`, `EvolMetrics`) |
   166→| `libs/inference` | EXTEND | Replace `get_llm()` with vLLM OpenAI-compatible loader; add `adapter_loader.py` |
   167→| `libs/model-training` | EXTEND | Add `peft_utils.py`, `trajectory.py`, `config.py` stubs |
   168→| `libs/data-pipeline` | KEEP | Stub; leave as is; repurposing is trivial later |
   169→| `libs/evaluation` | KEEP | Stub; leave as is |
   170→| `libs/events-py` | KEEP | Unchanged |
   171→| `apps/hitl-ui` | EXTEND | Add `src/rune/` feature directory with SessionView + AdapterInspector |
   172→
   173→### New Components to Create
   174→
   175→| Component | Type | Notes |
   176→|-----------|------|-------|
   177→| `libs/adapter-registry` | uv workspace lib | Foundation; all other new components import from here |
   178→| `services/lora-server` | Dockerfile + shell script only | NOT a uv workspace member; docker-compose service |
   179→| `services/training-svc` | uv workspace service | Depends on adapter-registry + model-training |
   180→| `services/evolution-svc` | uv workspace service | Depends on adapter-registry |
   181→
   182→### Build Order (Enforced by Import Dependencies)
   183→
   184→```
   185→Step 1:  Remove agent-b-service
   186→         (grep all references first; remove from workspace → uv lock → uv sync → delete dir)
   187→
   188→Step 2:  Rename agent-a-service → rune-agent
   189→         (git mv; update pyproject.toml name; update src dir; update all imports; update root pyproject.toml)
   190→
   191→Step 3:  Scaffold libs/adapter-registry
   192→         (GATE: everything else is blocked until this exists and is importable)
   193→
   194→Step 4:  Extend libs/shared with rune_models.py
   195→         (CodingSession, AdapterRef, EvolMetrics; no new workspace deps)
   196→
   197→Step 5:  Extend libs/model-training with PEFT stubs
   198→         (peft_utils.py, trajectory.py, config.py; no GPU imports; no new workspace deps)
   199→
   200→Step 6:  Update libs/inference loader
   201→         (get_llm() → ChatOpenAI pointing at lora-server; add adapter_loader.py; add langchain-openai dep)
   202→
   203→Step 7:  Extend services/api-service
   204→         (add routers/ directory; add adapter-registry workspace dep; update alembic/env.py imports)
   205→
   206→Step 8:  Scaffold services/lora-server
   207→         (Dockerfile + startup.sh + config.yaml + FastAPI sidecar; do NOT add to uv workspace members)
   208→
   209→Step 9:  Scaffold services/training-svc
   210→         (uv workspace member; add adapter-registry + model-training deps)
   211→
   212→Step 10: Scaffold services/evolution-svc
   213→         (uv workspace member; add adapter-registry dep)
   214→
   215→Step 11: Update services/rune-agent
   216→         (replace stub nodes with Rune-specific state/graph/nodes; add all lib deps)
   217→
   218→Step 12: Update apps/hitl-ui
   219→         (add src/rune/ feature directory; no npm package changes needed)
   220→
   221→Step 13: Update infra/docker-compose.yml

   223→
   224→Step 14: Update mkdocs.yml

   226→```
   227→
   228→### Root pyproject.toml — Five Sections Requiring Atomic Updates
   229→
   230→All five must be updated together or CI breaks silently:
   231→
   232→1. `[tool.uv.workspace] members` — add new members, remove old
   233→2. `[tool.mypy.overrides] module` — replace `agent_a_service`, `agent_b_service` with `rune_agent`, `training_service`, `evolution_service`, `adapter_registry`
   234→3. `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath` — add all new `src/` paths
   235→4. `[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths` — current `["services", "libs"]` auto-includes new dirs; verify it still applies
   236→5. `[tool.coverage.run] source` — mirror pythonpath changes exactly
   237→
   238→Makefile `typecheck` target upgrade (do this now, before adding any new services):
   239→```makefile
   240→typecheck:
   241→    uv run mypy services/*/src libs/*/src
   242→```
   243→This eliminates the primary vector for silent CI type-checking gaps.
   244→
   245→---
   246→
   247→## Key Pitfalls
   248→
   249→### Pitfall 1: uv Lockfile Must Be Regenerated at Every Workspace Member Change
   250→
   251→The uv workspace shares a single `uv.lock`. Removing a directory before running `uv lock` causes `uv sync` to fail with a package-not-found error that looks like a network issue. Adding a package before `uv lock` leaves consumers unable to resolve the dep.
   252→
   253→**Removal order:** Remove `{ workspace = true }` source references → remove from consumer `dependencies` → remove from `[tool.uv.workspace] members` → `uv lock` → `uv sync` → delete directory.
   254→**Addition order:** Create directory + `pyproject.toml` → add to `members` → `uv lock` → add consumer deps → `uv sync`.
   255→
   256→Never commit partial states. Run `uv lock && uv sync` before every commit during restructuring. Expect to run this cycle 8-10 times across the 14 build steps.
   257→
   258→### Pitfall 2: Four Names Per Package, All Must Match Independently
   259→
   260→Each Python package in this workspace has four independently-managed names. All four must be updated when renaming, or different failures appear at different times:
   261→
   262→| Location | Example | Breaks If Missed |
   263→|----------|---------|-----------------|
   264→| Directory path under `services/` or `libs/` | `libs/adapter-registry/` | uv workspace glob fails |
   265→| Python import path under `src/` | `src/adapter_registry/` | `ModuleNotFoundError` at runtime |
   266→| `[project] name` in `pyproject.toml` | `name = "adapter-registry"` | `[tool.uv.sources]` resolution fails |
   267→| `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages` | `packages = ["src/adapter_registry"]` | Editable install points at wrong dir |
   268→
   269→Critical nuance: `[tool.uv.sources]` keys must use hyphens matching `[project] name` exactly. uv does NOT normalize `adapter_registry = { workspace = true }` to `adapter-registry`. Only PyPI normalizes hyphens; uv sources does not.
   270→
   271→### Pitfall 3: Root pyproject.toml Has Five Hardcoded Path Lists That Drift Silently
   272→
   273→Forgetting `[tool.mypy.overrides]` means new services are never type-checked (silent safety hole). Forgetting `pythonpath` means pytest cannot find tests. Forgetting `coverage.source` underreports metrics. None of these produce immediate errors.
   274→
   275→The Makefile `typecheck` target currently hardcodes each component path. Adding `rune-agent` but forgetting the Makefile means mypy never runs on it in CI. Switching to `uv run mypy services/*/src libs/*/src` eliminates this entire category of failure.
   276→
   277→### Pitfall 4: GPU Imports at Module Level Break CI
   278→
   279→`torch`, `peft`, `bitsandbytes`, and `transformers` must never appear at module level in any new component. CI has no GPU. An accidental `import torch` at the top of `adapter_registry/models.py` will fail every CI run immediately.
   280→
   281→**Rule:** Scaffold deps must be installable without CUDA. GPU deps (`torch`, `vllm`, `peft`, `trl`, `bitsandbytes`) belong only in `training-svc` full implementation, locked behind Docker environment gating. The test suite must confirm each new component is importable without a GPU.
   282→
   283→### Pitfall 5: vLLM Must Be Launched as a Subprocess, Not Imported as a Python Dep
   284→
   285→Adding `vllm` to any service's `pyproject.toml` dependencies pulls in `torch` and CUDA transitively, breaking all non-GPU environments and CI. vLLM is launched via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec("vllm", "serve", ...)`. The `openai` package is the only dependency needed to communicate with vLLM's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This architectural boundary must be enforced at scaffold time — it is difficult to undo.
   286→
   287→**Bonus Blackwell pitfall:** On dual RTX 5090 (PCIe-connected, no NVLink), never use `tensor_parallel_size=2`. TP=2 over PCIe is slower than TP=1 and triggers a confirmed vLLM bug (Issue #21471) that corrupts LoRA adapter outputs. Use `pipeline_parallel_size=2, tensor_parallel_size=1` exclusively. The `LoraServerConfig` scaffold should raise `ValueError` on `tensor_parallel_size=2` to encode this constraint permanently.
   288→
   289→---
   290→
   291→## Recommendations
   292→
   293→### What the Roadmap Should Prioritize
   294→
   295→**1. Lockfile discipline is the critical path of the restructuring.** Plan to run `uv lock && uv sync` 8-10 times across 14 build steps. The development loop must be: one structural change → lock → sync → verify → commit → next step. Batching workspace member changes causes hard-to-diagnose failures.
   296→
   297→**2. Build `libs/adapter-registry` first, unconditionally.** It is the sole dependency root. Every other new component imports from it. Treat it as the prerequisite gate before any other new component is scaffolded.
   298→
   299→**3. The rename (agent-a → rune-agent) is safer and faster than creating from scratch.** The existing `agent-a-service` has the exact LangGraph skeleton (`state.py`, `graph.py`, `nodes.py`) that `rune-agent` needs. Renaming preserves structure, patterns, and git history. Do the rename before creating any new services.
   300→
   301→**4. Defer all Blackwell/GPU complexity to implementation phases.** The scaffold milestone is completable entirely on CPU. PyTorch nightly, source-built vLLM, and Unsloth Docker are real constraints but are not needed until Phase 2+ implementation work. Do not let GPU setup block scaffold delivery.
   302→
   303→**5. Switch the Makefile `typecheck` target to a glob immediately.** The current explicit list will drift the moment the first new service is added. `uv run mypy services/*/src libs/*/src` takes 30 seconds to implement and eliminates the primary vector for silent CI type-safety gaps during all future work.
   304→
   305→**6. Follow the build order strictly.** Steps 1-14 match the import dependency DAG. Every component can be imported as soon as it is scaffolded. Skipping ahead creates unresolvable import errors that are confusing to debug.
   306→
   307→**7. The base model decision is settled for implementation phases.** Use Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct: fits in QLoRA on a single RTX 5090 (~12-14GB), native HuggingFace support (PEFT/vLLM work out of the box), Apache 2.0 license, 61.6% HumanEval. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B is the drop-in alternative for stronger reasoning at identical VRAM footprint.
   308→
   309→---
   310→
   311→## Open Questions
   312→
   313→These decisions were not resolved by research and require user input before or during implementation:
   314→
   315→| Question | Context | When Needed |
   316→|----------|---------|-------------|
   317→| **Dramatiq vs FastAPI BackgroundTasks at scaffold time** | Research recommends Dramatiq[redis] for full async job isolation in training-svc, but BackgroundTasks is sufficient for scaffold and avoids a Redis service dependency. | Before Step 9 (training-svc scaffold) |
   318→| **Adapter filesystem path convention** | Research assumes `~/.rune/adapters/` as base. Should scaffold encode this as `RUNE_ADAPTER_PATH` env var? | Before Step 3 (adapter-registry scaffold) |
   319→| **libs/data-pipeline and libs/evaluation disposition** | Both are empty stubs. Rune's training data loading belongs in `training-svc`; fitness evaluation belongs in `evolution-svc`. Should they be removed to reduce workspace noise, or kept as integration stubs? | Before Step 1 (affects component count) |
   320→| **Sandbox strategy for code execution** | `rune-agent`'s `execute_node` needs a sandbox. Options: subprocess (no new dep, scaffold-appropriate), E2B Firecracker microVMs (`e2b` PyPI, 150ms startup, cloud), Modal. Scaffold uses subprocess; choice affects Phase 3 deps. | Before Phase 3 (rune-agent implementation) |
   321→| **SGLang vs vLLM as primary inference engine** | SGLang 0.4.x is 29% faster than vLLM 0.16.x in 2026 benchmarks and better for structured/agent outputs. Decision affects `startup.sh` and `VLLMClient` design. | Before Phase 2 (lora-server implementation) |
   322→| **LMCache adoption timeline** | LMCache provides 3-10x latency reduction on multi-turn agent loops. Add with vLLM in Phase 2, or wait until Phase 3 after baseline works? | Before Phase 2 or Phase 3 |
   323→| **Doc-to-LoRA vs SHINE hypernetwork** | SakanaAI/doc-to-lora (MIT, uv-managed) vs Yewei-Liu/SHINE (single forward pass, frozen LLM representations). Both published Feb 2026. Choice affects Phase 4 architecture. | Before Phase 4 (hypernetwork implementation) |
   324→

   332→

### Derivation Notes

The phase structure follows the import dependency DAG strictly:

- Phase 4 (Cleanup) must come first — it removes `agent-b-service` and renames `agent-a-service` to `rune-agent` before any new workspace members are added. Adding new members before removing old ones causes lockfile resolution failures that are hard to diagnose.
- Phase 5 (Foundation Libraries) is gated on Phase 4 completing because `libs/adapter-registry` (LIB-01) is the sole dependency root — every new service imports from it. It cannot be scaffolded while the workspace still contains dead references from the template.
- Phase 6 (Service Scaffolds) merges CFG-01 and CFG-02 with the service work because the root `pyproject.toml` five-section atomic update must happen alongside the service additions, not after. Separating workspace config from the services that trigger it creates a phase that cannot be independently verified.
- Phase 7 (Quality Gate) is terminal and intentionally contains the docker-compose and mkdocs work alongside the QA requirements. These have no further dependencies and are correctly positioned as the final verification sweep before the milestone closes.

### Phase 1: README
**Goal**: A polished README.md exists that anyone can read to understand what Rune is, how it works, what hardware it needs, where the project stands, and which papers it builds on
**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)
**Requirements**: DOC-01, DOC-02, DOC-03, DOC-04, DOC-05
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. A reader new to Rune can explain the core innovation (parametric episodic memory via LoRA) and how it differs from Aider, Cursor, and Claude Code after reading the README
  2. The architecture overview section describes the recursive loop, hypernetwork, evolution operator, and adapter serving — with a diagram or structured visual representation of data flow
  3. The hardware requirements section lists specific prerequisites (dual RTX 4090, CUDA 12.8+, PyTorch nightly cu128, QLoRA) so a developer knows before cloning whether they can run Rune
  4. The current status section honestly states that no implementation exists, this is a research-stage project, and the core hypothesis (Doc-to-LoRA on coding trajectories) is unvalidated
  5. The references section cites Doc-to-LoRA (arXiv:2602.15902), S-LoRA (arXiv:2311.03285), and QLoRA (arXiv:2305.14314) with links
**Plans**: 1/1 plans complete

Plans:
- [x] 01-01-PLAN.md — Write complete README.md (vision, architecture diagrams, hardware, status, references)

### Phase 2: Implementation Plan
**Goal**: A detailed, phased implementation plan document exists that transforms the Rune architecture specification into actionable phases with pass/fail criteria, risk gates, and a concrete build order grounded in hardware reality
**Depends on**: Phase 1
**Requirements**: PLAN-01, PLAN-02, PLAN-03, PLAN-04, PLAN-05, PLAN-06
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. Phase 0 of the implementation plan defines hardware and environment validation with specific pass/fail criteria (both GPUs recognized, PyTorch nightly cu128 forward+backward pass without segfault, vLLM serving Qwen2.5-Coder-7B via pipeline parallelism without TP+LoRA corruption)
  2. Phase 1 of the implementation plan is structured as a kill-switch gate: it defines a measurable success threshold (at minimum, 5% Pass@1 improvement on held-out HumanEval tasks) and states explicitly that no infrastructure is built if this gate fails
  3. Every subsequent phase in the plan states its deliverables, which previous phase it depends on, and the success criteria that mark it complete
  4. The plan explicitly addresses the three primary research risks: adapter composition interference (heterogeneous subspaces), hypernetwork mode collapse (mean-adapter collapse), and catastrophic forgetting (non-immutable adapter writes) — each with a mitigation strategy
  5. The plan reflects the hardware reality: dual RTX 4090 with CXL, pipeline parallelism (PP=2) not tensor parallelism, QLoRA as required for 24GB per-GPU constraint, with QLoRA introduced only after Phase 1 bfloat16 baseline passes
  6. The plan includes the recommended build order: adapter-registry → lora-server → model-training extensions → api-service extensions → rune-agent → evolution-svc → training-svc → hypernetwork
**Plans**: 2/2 plans complete

Plans:
- [x] 02-01-PLAN.md — Clean MkDocs config, replace landing page, write risk matrix and build order appendices
- [x] 02-02-PLAN.md — Write main implementation plan document (5 phases, kill-switch gate, executive summary)

### Phase 3: Architecture Docs
**Goal**: Internal architecture documentation exists covering the four core design decisions that implementation will depend on: the recursive code generation loop, how Rune maps to the existing monorepo, the adapter storage strategy, and the multi-GPU inference and training strategy
**Depends on**: Phase 2
**Requirements**: ARCH-01, ARCH-02, ARCH-03, ARCH-04
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. The recursive code generation loop document shows explicit data flow: what enters each step (generate, execute, reflect, distill), what exits, what triggers a retry, and what terminates the loop
  2. The monorepo mapping document lists each new Rune service (rune-agent, lora-server, training-svc, evolution-svc, adapter-registry) alongside the existing monorepo service it extends or runs alongside, with integration points named
  3. The adapter storage strategy document specifies the filesystem path convention, the SQLite schema fields (at minimum: id, version, task_type, created_at, file_path, pass_rate), and the write-once enforcement policy
  4. The multi-GPU strategy document specifies pipeline parallelism (PP=2, TP=1) as the required configuration, explains why tensor parallelism is excluded (confirmed vLLM bug #21471, no NVLink on consumer Blackwell), and documents the GPU lease mechanism for coordinating concurrent training and serving
**Plans**: 1/1 plans complete

### Documentation

- [x] **DOC-02**: README.md includes architecture overview diagram (recursive loop, hypernetwork, evolution operator, adapter serving)
- [x] **DOC-03**: README.md includes hardware requirements and getting-started prerequisites
- [x] **DOC-04**: README.md includes current status section with honest assessment of research stage

### Implementation Plan

- [x] **PLAN-01**: Phase 0 defines hardware/environment validation with specific pass/fail criteria
- [x] **PLAN-02**: Phase 1 defines core hypothesis validation as kill-switch gate (Doc-to-LoRA on coding tasks)
- [x] **PLAN-03**: Each subsequent phase has clear deliverables, dependencies, and success criteria
- [x] **PLAN-04**: Plan addresses key research risks: adapter composition interference, hypernetwork mode collapse, catastrophic forgetting
- [x] **PLAN-05**: Plan reflects hardware reality: dual RTX 4090 + CXL, pipeline parallelism (not tensor), QLoRA required
- [x] **PLAN-06**: Plan includes suggested build order from architecture research (adapter-registry → lora-server → api-extensions → rune-agent → evolution → training)

### Architecture Documentation

- [x] **ARCH-01**: Document the recursive code generation loop with data flow
- [x] **ARCH-02**: Document how Rune components map to existing monorepo services

## v2 Requirements

Requirements for milestone v2.0 — Repo Restructuring & Scaffold.

### Cleanup

- [ ] **CLN-01**: Template placeholder service `agent-b-service` is removed from the workspace (directory deleted, all references in root pyproject.toml removed, uv lock/sync passes)
- [ ] **CLN-02**: Template placeholder service `agent-a-service` is renamed to `rune-agent` with all four name locations updated (directory, src/ module, pyproject.toml name, hatch wheel packages)
- [ ] **CLN-03**: Root pyproject.toml dev dependencies are cleaned of unused template packages (google-cloud-aiplatform, vertexai, google-genai, sentence-transformers) and GPU packages are moved out of root scope
- [ ] **CLN-04**: Makefile typecheck target uses glob pattern (`services/*/src libs/*/src`) instead of hardcoded component list

### Scaffold — Libraries

- [ ] **LIB-01**: `libs/adapter-registry` exists as a uv workspace member with SQLModel `AdapterRecord` schema, stub CRUD methods (`store`, `retrieve_by_id`, `query_by_task_type`, `list_all`), and custom exceptions (`AdapterAlreadyExistsError`, `AdapterNotFoundError`)
- [ ] **LIB-02**: `libs/shared` is extended with `rune_models.py` containing Rune-specific Pydantic models (`CodingSession`, `AdapterRef`, `EvolMetrics`)
- [ ] **LIB-03**: `libs/model-training` is extended with stub modules (`peft_utils.py`, `trajectory.py`, `config.py`) containing typed function signatures that raise `NotImplementedError`
- [ ] **LIB-04**: `libs/inference` is extended with `adapter_loader.py` stub and updated loader pointing at vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Scaffold — Services

- [ ] **SVC-01**: `services/rune-agent` has a LangGraph `StateGraph` with `RuneState`, four nodes (generate, execute, reflect, save_trajectory), conditional edges, and a working `should_retry` function
- [ ] **SVC-02**: `services/lora-server` exists as a Dockerfile-only service (NOT a uv workspace member) with startup script, config enforcing PP=2/TP=1, FastAPI health sidecar, and `VLLMClient` stub
- [ ] **SVC-03**: `services/training-svc` exists as a uv workspace service with FastAPI endpoints (`/train/lora`, `/train/hypernetwork`, `/jobs/{job_id}`), request schemas, and `TrainingJob` SQLModel
- [ ] **SVC-04**: `services/evolution-svc` exists as a uv workspace service with FastAPI endpoints (`/evaluate`, `/evolve`, `/promote`, `/prune`), evaluation schemas, and stub lifecycle manager
- [ ] **SVC-05**: `services/api-service` is extended with `/adapters` and `/sessions` router stubs (501 responses) wired into main.py

### Configuration

- [ ] **CFG-01**: Root pyproject.toml workspace members list includes all new components and excludes removed ones; all five hardcoded path sections (workspace members, mypy overrides, pytest pythonpath, testpaths, coverage source) are consistent

- [ ] **CFG-03**: `infra/docker-compose.yml` includes lora-server container definition with GPU passthrough and adapter volume mount
- [ ] **CFG-04**: `mkdocs.yml` nav reflects the new component structure; `uv run mkdocs build` passes

### Quality

- [ ] **QA-01**: Every new component has at least one test confirming importability without GPU; `uv run pytest` passes across the full workspace
- [ ] **QA-02**: No GPU imports (`torch`, `peft`, `bitsandbytes`, `transformers`, `vllm`) appear at module level in any scaffold component
- [ ] **QA-03**: `uv run ruff check .` passes cleanly across all new and modified components
- [ ] **QA-04**: All API route stubs return HTTP 501 (Not Implemented), not 200 with fake data

### Key Design Decisions

- **Sequential waves** (not parallel): All plans modify `pyproject.toml`, and the STATE.md decision says "Remove agent-b-service before any other workspace changes to avoid lockfile conflicts"
- **Plan 01 is a single task**: Removing agent-b-service is straightforward but touches many files -- combining into one task avoids artificial splits
- **Plan 02 splits into 2 tasks**: Task 1 handles the service-internal rename (git mv, module rename, pyproject.toml name changes), Task 2 handles all external references (root config, CI, docs). This separates concerns and each task is self-verifiable
- **Plan 03 combines CLN-03 + CLN-04**: Both are small, independent changes to different files (pyproject.toml deps vs Makefile/CI patterns) that naturally fit in one plan

However, there's a nuance: the `rune_agent`/`rune_agent.*` entries need to be in the mypy overrides list after plan 04-02 renames agent-a-service. **Confirmed gap: plan 04-02 does NOT address the `.github/copilot-instructions.md` re: the mypy overrides for `rune_agent`.** Wait — plan 04-02 Task 2 step 8 explicitly says: "In `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, update `services/agent-a-service/` to `services/rune-agent/`". This IS covered.

Let me verify one more potential gap — the `monorepo-mapping.md` line 17 "Runs alongside `agent-a-service`, `agent-b-service`" — after plan 04-01 removes agent-b-service reference from that line (plan 04-01 step 6, third sub-bullet), the line becomes "Runs alongside `agent-a-service`". Then plan 04-02 would update agent-a-service → rune-agent in that line. But plan 04-02 step 6 says "The rune-agent row already exists and references `services/rune-agent/` — verify this is correct / Remove the old `agent-a-service` row from the 'Existing services' table / Update the directory tree." It does NOT explicitly mention updating line 17's "Runs alongside" cell. This is a potential gap.

However, the comprehensive grep in plan 04-02 Task 2 step 10 would catch this: `grep -rn "agent.a.service\|agent_a_service"` over docs/ should catch line 17's `agent-a-service` mention. So while not explicitly called out, the verify step would expose it and the instruction says "zero matches."

### Phase 1: README
**Goal**: A polished README.md exists that anyone can read to understand what Rune is, how it works, what hardware it needs, where the project stands, and which papers it builds on
**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)
**Requirements**: DOC-01, DOC-02, DOC-03, DOC-04, DOC-05
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. A reader new to Rune can explain the core innovation (parametric episodic memory via LoRA) and how it differs from Aider, Cursor, and Claude Code after reading the README
  2. The architecture overview section describes the recursive loop, hypernetwork, evolution operator, and adapter serving — with a diagram or structured visual representation of data flow
  3. The hardware requirements section lists specific prerequisites (dual RTX 4090, CUDA 12.8+, PyTorch nightly cu128, QLoRA) so a developer knows before cloning whether they can run Rune
  4. The current status section honestly states that no implementation exists, this is a research-stage project, and the core hypothesis (Doc-to-LoRA on coding trajectories) is unvalidated
  5. The references section cites Doc-to-LoRA (arXiv:2602.15902), S-LoRA (arXiv:2311.03285), and QLoRA (arXiv:2305.14314) with links
**Plans**: 1/1 plans complete

Plans:
- [x] 01-01-PLAN.md — Write complete README.md (vision, architecture diagrams, hardware, status, references)

### Phase 2: Implementation Plan
**Goal**: A detailed, phased implementation plan document exists that transforms the Rune architecture specification into actionable phases with pass/fail criteria, risk gates, and a concrete build order grounded in hardware reality
**Depends on**: Phase 1
**Requirements**: PLAN-01, PLAN-02, PLAN-03, PLAN-04, PLAN-05, PLAN-06
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. Phase 0 of the implementation plan defines hardware and environment validation with specific pass/fail criteria (both GPUs recognized, PyTorch nightly cu128 forward+backward pass without segfault, vLLM serving Qwen2.5-Coder-7B via pipeline parallelism without TP+LoRA corruption)
  2. Phase 1 of the implementation plan is structured as a kill-switch gate: it defines a measurable success threshold (at minimum, 5% Pass@1 improvement on held-out HumanEval tasks) and states explicitly that no infrastructure is built if this gate fails
  3. Every subsequent phase in the plan states its deliverables, which previous phase it depends on, and the success criteria that mark it complete
  4. The plan explicitly addresses the three primary research risks: adapter composition interference (heterogeneous subspaces), hypernetwork mode collapse (mean-adapter collapse), and catastrophic forgetting (non-immutable adapter writes) — each with a mitigation strategy
  5. The plan reflects the hardware reality: dual RTX 4090 with CXL, pipeline parallelism (PP=2) not tensor parallelism, QLoRA as required for 24GB per-GPU constraint, with QLoRA introduced only after Phase 1 bfloat16 baseline passes
  6. The plan includes the recommended build order: adapter-registry → lora-server → model-training extensions → api-service extensions → rune-agent → evolution-svc → training-svc → hypernetwork
**Plans**: 2/2 plans complete

Plans:
- [x] 02-01-PLAN.md — Clean MkDocs config, replace landing page, write risk matrix and build order appendices
- [x] 02-02-PLAN.md — Write main implementation plan document (5 phases, kill-switch gate, executive summary)

### Phase 3: Architecture Docs
**Goal**: Internal architecture documentation exists covering the four core design decisions that implementation will depend on: the recursive code generation loop, how Rune maps to the existing monorepo, the adapter storage strategy, and the multi-GPU inference and training strategy
**Depends on**: Phase 2
**Requirements**: ARCH-01, ARCH-02, ARCH-03, ARCH-04
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. The recursive code generation loop document shows explicit data flow: what enters each step (generate, execute, reflect, distill), what exits, what triggers a retry, and what terminates the loop
  2. The monorepo mapping document lists each new Rune service (rune-agent, lora-server, training-svc, evolution-svc, adapter-registry) alongside the existing monorepo service it extends or runs alongside, with integration points named
  3. The adapter storage strategy document specifies the filesystem path convention, the SQLite schema fields (at minimum: id, version, task_type, created_at, file_path, pass_rate), and the write-once enforcement policy
  4. The multi-GPU strategy document specifies pipeline parallelism (PP=2, TP=1) as the required configuration, explains why tensor parallelism is excluded (confirmed vLLM bug #21471, no NVLink on consumer Blackwell), and documents the GPU lease mechanism for coordinating concurrent training and serving
**Plans**: 1/1 plans complete

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Phase:** 05 - Foundation Libraries
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- **Three libs exist, one must be created from scratch.** `shared`, `model-training`, and `inference` are already workspace members needing additive files only. `adapter-registry` is net-new and is the hard gate for Phase 6.
- **`uv init --lib` auto-adds the new member** to `[tool.uv.workspace]` in the root `pyproject.toml`, but generates `uv_build` as the build backend — this must be replaced with hatchling immediately to match the workspace convention.
- **`openai` is not in the lockfile.** The `inference` lib's new `adapter_loader.py` must use the `openai` package (not `vllm` directly), and `openai` must be added to `libs/inference/pyproject.toml` deps before `uv lock` can pass.
- **Five config sections in root `pyproject.toml` need updating** when adding `adapter-registry`: workspace members, mypy overrides, pytest pythonpath, testpaths, and coverage source. Missing any one causes silent failures.
- **`SQLModel table=True` is CPU-safe for import** but requires an explicit `__tablename__ = "adapter_records"` to avoid `InvalidRequestError` collisions with existing `entity` and `task` tables in `shared.models`.

### File Created

`/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/rune/.planning/phases/05-foundation-libraries/05-RESEARCH.md`

### Confidence Assessment

| Area | Level | Reason |
|------|-------|--------|
| Standard Stack | HIGH | All packages verified live in lockfile + Context7 official docs |
| Architecture | HIGH | Pattern derived from existing libs (events-py reference impl) + official uv/SQLModel docs |
| Pitfalls | HIGH | Most verified by direct source code inspection of the working tree; one (uv_build backend) flagged MEDIUM as uv version-dependent |

### Open Questions

1. Whether `adapter-registry` should also declare `shared` as a dependency (recommendation: no, defer to Phase 6)
2. Whether `loaders.py` needs a new function or if `adapter_loader.py` alone satisfies "updated loader" (recommendation: `adapter_loader.py` is sufficient)
3. Whether `peft`/`bitsandbytes` should be added as `model-training` deps now (recommendation: no, stubs don't need them and they'd risk breaking CPU sync)

### Ready for Planning

     1→# Phase 5: Foundation Libraries - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-03-02
     4→**Domain:** uv workspace packaging, SQLModel schema design, Pydantic v2 models, deferred GPU imports, OpenAI-compatible inference client
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 5 creates four library scaffolds that must be importable on CPU-only machines. Three of the four libraries (`shared`, `model-training`, `inference`) already exist as uv workspace members and need additive file changes only. The fourth (`adapter-registry`) is a net-new library that must be created from scratch, added to the workspace members list, and locked. The hard gate is `adapter-registry` — all future services import it, so it must pass importability before Phase 6 scaffolding can proceed.
    10→
    11→The key constraint across all four libraries is zero GPU-dependent imports at module level. `model-training` already has `torch>=2.0.0` in its dependencies and torch is already in `uv.lock`; however, the three new stub modules (`peft_utils.py`, `trajectory.py`, `config.py`) must use `TYPE_CHECKING` guards or lazy imports for any GPU library references. For `inference`, the existing `loaders.py` uses a lazy Vertex AI pattern — the new `adapter_loader.py` should use the same lazy-import approach but targeting the `openai` package with a configurable `base_url`. `openai` is not currently in the workspace lockfile, so the `inference` pyproject.toml must declare it as a dependency.
    12→
    13→The `adapter-registry` library is the most complex deliverable: it needs a full hatchling-backed `pyproject.toml`, a `src/adapter_registry/` package layout, a SQLModel table model (`AdapterRecord`), two custom exceptions, four stub CRUD methods, and a clean `__init__.py` that exports the public surface. SQLModel 0.0.37 (already in the root lockfile) supports `table=True` models, so the `AdapterRecord` schema can use the documented field patterns. Importability without GPU is guaranteed because SQLModel's only dependency is SQLAlchemy + Pydantic, both CPU-only.
    14→
    15→**Primary recommendation:** Create `adapter-registry` as a standalone library package using `uv init --lib libs/adapter-registry` (which auto-adds it to the workspace), then write the SQLModel schema and stubs. Add `adapter-registry` as a workspace dependency to the root `pyproject.toml`, run `uv lock && uv sync` once, then make the additive changes to the three existing libs.

    74→## Architecture Patterns
    75→
    76→### Recommended Project Structure — adapter-registry (new)
    77→
    78→```
    79→libs/adapter-registry/
    80→├── README.md
    81→├── pyproject.toml          # name="adapter-registry", hatchling, sqlmodel dep
    82→└── src/

    84→        ├── __init__.py     # exports: AdapterRecord, AdapterRegistry, errors
    85→        ├── models.py       # SQLModel AdapterRecord (table=True)
    86→        ├── registry.py     # AdapterRegistry class with 4 stub methods
    87→        └── exceptions.py   # AdapterAlreadyExistsError, AdapterNotFoundError
    88→```
    89→
    90→### Recommended Structure — additive files (existing libs)
    91→
    92→```
    93→libs/shared/src/shared/
    94→└── rune_models.py          # CodingSession, AdapterRef, EvolMetrics (Pydantic)
    95→
    96→libs/model-training/src/model_training/
    97→├── peft_utils.py           # typed stubs, raise NotImplementedError
    98→├── trajectory.py           # typed stubs, raise NotImplementedError
    99→└── config.py               # typed stubs, raise NotImplementedError
   100→
   101→libs/inference/src/inference/
   102→└── adapter_loader.py       # stub pointing at vLLM OpenAI endpoint
   103→```
   104→
   105→### Pattern 1: uv Workspace — Adding a New Library Member
   106→
   107→**What:** `uv init --lib` creates the package scaffold and automatically inserts the new member into `[tool.uv.workspace] members` in the root `pyproject.toml`. Running `uv lock && uv sync` after creation resolves and installs it.
   108→**When to use:** Every new Python library added to the monorepo.
   109→
   110→```bash
   111→# Source: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/init/
   112→# Run from repo root:
   113→uv init --lib libs/adapter-registry
   114→# This creates: libs/adapter-registry/pyproject.toml, src/adapter_registry/__init__.py
   115→# And adds "libs/adapter-registry" to [tool.uv.workspace] members in root pyproject.toml
   116→uv lock && uv sync
   117→```
   118→
   119→After `uv init --lib`, the `pyproject.toml` will use `uv_build` as the build backend. **Replace this with `hatchling`** to match all other libs in the workspace:
   120→
   121→```toml
   122→[build-system]
   123→requires = ["hatchling"]
   124→build-backend = "hatchling.build"
   125→
   126→[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
   127→packages = ["src/adapter_registry"]
   128→```
   129→
   130→### Pattern 2: SQLModel Table Model (AdapterRecord)
   131→
   132→**What:** SQLModel `table=True` class that maps to an SQLite row. Fields match the adapter-storage.md schema.
   133→**When to use:** The `AdapterRecord` in `libs/adapter-registry/src/adapter_registry/models.py`.
   134→
   135→```python
   136→# Source: Context7 /websites/sqlmodel_tiangolo
   137→from datetime import datetime
   138→from typing import Optional
   139→from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel
   140→
   141→
   142→class AdapterRecord(SQLModel, table=True):
   143→    """SQLite-backed metadata for a stored LoRA adapter."""
   144→
   145→    id: str = Field(primary_key=True)                    # UUID v4
   146→    version: int = Field()
   147→    task_type: str = Field(index=True)
   148→    base_model_id: str = Field()
   149→    rank: int = Field()
   150→    created_at: str = Field()                            # ISO 8601
   151→    file_path: str = Field()
   152→    file_hash: str = Field()
   153→    file_size_bytes: int = Field()
   154→    pass_rate: Optional[float] = Field(default=None)
   155→    fitness_score: Optional[float] = Field(default=None)
   156→    source: str = Field()                               # 'fine-tune' | 'hypernetwork'
   157→    session_id: str = Field()
   158→    is_archived: bool = Field(default=False)
   159→```
   160→
   161→Note: `table=True` triggers SQLAlchemy table registration at **class definition time**. This is a known pitfall: importing `AdapterRecord` causes SQLAlchemy metadata registration, but does NOT require a live database connection. CPU-only importability is safe as long as `create_engine` / `Session` calls are inside stub methods (which raise `NotImplementedError` anyway).
   162→
   163→### Pattern 3: Custom Exceptions
   164→
   165→**What:** Custom exception classes for domain-specific error handling in `adapter-registry`.
   166→**When to use:** `AdapterAlreadyExistsError` on duplicate `store`, `AdapterNotFoundError` on `retrieve_by_id` / `query_by_task_type` misses.
   167→
   168→```python
   169→# Source: standard Python exception pattern
   170→class AdapterRegistryError(Exception):
   171→    """Base exception for adapter registry operations."""
   172→    pass
   173→
   174→
   175→class AdapterAlreadyExistsError(AdapterRegistryError):
   176→    """Raised when attempting to store an adapter with a duplicate ID."""
   177→    pass
   178→
   179→
   180→class AdapterNotFoundError(AdapterRegistryError):
   181→    """Raised when an adapter matching the query criteria does not exist."""
   182→    pass
   183→```
   184→
   185→### Pattern 4: `__init__.py` Public Surface
   186→
   187→**What:** `adapter-registry`'s `__init__.py` re-exports everything the success criterion requires.
   188→
   189→```python
   190→# libs/adapter-registry/src/adapter_registry/__init__.py
   191→from adapter_registry.exceptions import AdapterAlreadyExistsError, AdapterNotFoundError
   192→from adapter_registry.models import AdapterRecord
   193→from adapter_registry.registry import AdapterRegistry
   194→
   195→__all__ = [
   196→    "AdapterRecord",
   197→    "AdapterRegistry",
   198→    "AdapterAlreadyExistsError",
   199→    "AdapterNotFoundError",
   200→]
   201→```
   202→
   203→Success criterion: `from adapter_registry import AdapterRecord, AdapterRegistry, AdapterAlreadyExistsError, AdapterNotFoundError` must succeed without GPU.
   204→
   205→### Pattern 5: AdapterRegistry Class with Stub CRUD
   206→
   207→**What:** Class containing four stub methods that raise `NotImplementedError` with descriptive messages.
   208→
   209→```python
   210→# libs/adapter-registry/src/adapter_registry/registry.py
   211→from adapter_registry.exceptions import AdapterAlreadyExistsError, AdapterNotFoundError
   212→from adapter_registry.models import AdapterRecord
   213→
   214→
   215→class AdapterRegistry:
   216→    """Registry for LoRA adapter metadata. Backed by SQLite via SQLModel."""
   217→
   218→    def store(self, record: AdapterRecord) -> None:
   219→        """Persist a new adapter record.
   220→
   221→        Args:
   222→            record: The AdapterRecord to store.
   223→
   224→        Raises:
   225→            AdapterAlreadyExistsError: If an adapter with the same ID already exists.
   226→            NotImplementedError: Always (stub — not yet implemented).
   227→        """
   228→        raise NotImplementedError(
   229→            "AdapterRegistry.store is not yet implemented. "
   230→            "It will insert the AdapterRecord into SQLite and verify ID uniqueness."
   231→        )
   232→
   233→    def retrieve_by_id(self, adapter_id: str) -> AdapterRecord:
   234→        """Retrieve a single adapter by its unique ID.
   235→
   236→        Args:
   237→            adapter_id: UUID v4 identifier of the adapter.
   238→
   239→        Raises:
   240→            AdapterNotFoundError: If no adapter with the given ID exists.
   241→            NotImplementedError: Always (stub — not yet implemented).
   242→        """
   243→        raise NotImplementedError(
   244→            "AdapterRegistry.retrieve_by_id is not yet implemented. "
   245→            "It will query SQLite for the adapter with the given ID."
   246→        )
   247→
   248→    def query_by_task_type(self, task_type: str) -> list[AdapterRecord]:
   249→        """Return all adapters matching the given task type.
   250→
   251→        Args:
   252→            task_type: Task category (e.g. 'bug-fix', 'feature-impl').
   253→
   254→        Raises:
   255→            NotImplementedError: Always (stub — not yet implemented).
   256→        """
   257→        raise NotImplementedError(
   258→            "AdapterRegistry.query_by_task_type is not yet implemented. "
   259→            "It will query SQLite filtered by task_type index."
   260→        )
   261→
   262→    def list_all(self) -> list[AdapterRecord]:
   263→        """Return all non-archived adapter records.
   264→
   265→        Raises:
   266→            NotImplementedError: Always (stub — not yet implemented).
   267→        """
   268→        raise NotImplementedError(
   269→            "AdapterRegistry.list_all is not yet implemented. "
   270→            "It will return all AdapterRecords where is_archived=False."
   271→        )
   272→```
   273→
   274→### Pattern 6: Pydantic v2 Models (`rune_models.py` in shared)
   275→
   276→**What:** Pure Pydantic BaseModel (not SQLModel table) for Rune-specific data structures.
   277→
   278→```python
   279→# libs/shared/src/shared/rune_models.py
   280→from typing import Optional
   281→from pydantic import BaseModel
   282→
   283→
   284→class AdapterRef(BaseModel):
   285→    """Reference to a stored LoRA adapter by ID and metadata."""
   286→    adapter_id: str
   287→    task_type: str
   288→    fitness_score: Optional[float] = None
   289→
   290→
   291→class CodingSession(BaseModel):
   292→    """A complete agent coding session: task in, trajectory out."""
   293→    session_id: str
   294→    task_description: str
   295→    task_type: str
   296→    adapter_refs: list[AdapterRef] = []
   297→    attempt_count: int = 0
   298→    outcome: Optional[str] = None  # 'success' | 'exhausted' | None
   299→
   300→
   301→class EvolMetrics(BaseModel):
   302→    """Evolution evaluation metrics for an adapter."""
   303→    adapter_id: str
   304→    pass_rate: float
   305→    fitness_score: float
   306→    generalization_delta: Optional[float] = None
   307→```

   309→### Pattern 7: OpenAI Client Pointing at vLLM (`adapter_loader.py` in inference)
   310→
   311→**What:** `adapter_loader.py` provides a stub `load_adapter` function and an `get_vllm_client()` helper that configures the `openai` client to hit the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The `openai` package is CPU-safe; it makes HTTP calls but does not depend on CUDA.
   312→
   313→```python
   314→# libs/inference/src/inference/adapter_loader.py
   315→# Source: Context7 /openai/openai-python — base_url pattern
   316→from typing import Any
   317→from openai import AsyncOpenAI
   318→
   319→
   320→VLLM_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000/v1"  # configurable via env var
   321→
   322→
   323→def get_vllm_client(base_url: str = VLLM_BASE_URL) -> AsyncOpenAI:
   324→    """Return an AsyncOpenAI client pointed at the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
   325→
   326→    The client uses the openai package (NOT a direct vllm import) so it can
   327→    be instantiated on CPU-only machines.
   328→
   329→    Args:
   330→        base_url: Base URL of the vLLM server (default: localhost:8000/v1).
   331→
   332→    Returns:
   333→        Configured AsyncOpenAI client.
   334→    """
   335→    return AsyncOpenAI(
   336→        base_url=base_url,
   337→        api_key=[REDACTED]",  # vLLM local ignores API key
   338→    )
   339→
   340→
   341→def load_adapter(adapter_id: str, model_name: str) -> Any:
   342→    """Load a LoRA adapter into the vLLM serving process.
   343→
   344→    Args:
   345→        adapter_id: UUID of the adapter to load.
   346→        model_name: Base model identifier.
   347→
   348→    Raises:
   349→        NotImplementedError: Always (stub — not yet implemented).
   350→    """
   351→    raise NotImplementedError(
   352→        "load_adapter is not yet implemented. "
   353→        "It will call the vLLM dynamic LoRA loading API via the openai client."
   354→    )
   355→```
   356→
   357→The existing `loaders.py` must also be updated to add a `get_vllm_loader` function (or update to reference `adapter_loader.get_vllm_client`). The requirement says the inference loader "points at the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint." The cleanest interpretation: `adapter_loader.py` is the new module, and `loaders.py` is updated to import from it or document the new path.
   358→
   359→### Pattern 8: GPU-safe Stub Pattern for `model-training`
   360→
   361→**What:** New stub modules in `model-training` must not import `torch`, `peft`, `bitsandbytes`, or `transformers` at module level.
   362→
   363→```python
   364→# libs/model-training/src/model_training/peft_utils.py
   365→# NO top-level: import torch / from peft import ...
   366→from typing import Any, Optional
   367→
   368→
   369→def build_qlora_config(
   370→    rank: int,
   371→    alpha: int,
   372→    target_modules: list[str],
   373→    dropout: float = 0.1,
   374→) -> Any:
   375→    """Build a QLoRA PEFT configuration.
   376→
   377→    Args:
   378→        rank: LoRA rank (e.g. 64).
   379→        alpha: LoRA alpha scaling factor.
   380→        target_modules: List of attention module names to target.
   381→        dropout: LoRA dropout rate.
   382→
   383→    Returns:
   384→        Configured LoraConfig instance.
   385→
   386→    Raises:
   387→        NotImplementedError: Always (stub — not yet implemented).
   388→    """
   389→    raise NotImplementedError(
   390→        "build_qlora_config is not yet implemented. "
   391→        "It will instantiate peft.LoraConfig with QLoRA quantization settings."
   392→    )
   393→```
   394→
   395→If a function needs to TYPE-CHECK a torch type without importing at module level:
   396→```python
   397→from __future__ import annotations
   398→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
   399→if TYPE_CHECKING:
   400→    import torch
   401→```
   402→
   403→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   404→
   405→- **`table=True` with conflicting table names:** SQLModel raises a `SAWarning` / `InvalidRequestError` if two `table=True` models share the same `__tablename__`. Use explicit `__tablename__` in `AdapterRecord` if there's any collision risk with existing `Entity`/`Task` models in `shared`.
   406→- **Importing `torch` at top of stub files:** Even `import torch` at module level will fail if torch CUDA isn't installed properly. Use lazy imports or `TYPE_CHECKING` guards.
   407→- **Forgetting `__all__` in `__init__.py`:** The success criterion checks a specific import; `__all__` makes the public surface explicit and prevents accidental imports from breaking ruff/mypy.
   408→- **`uv init --lib` default build backend:** `uv init --lib` now generates `uv_build` as the build backend (not hatchling). All existing libs use hatchling. Switch the generated `pyproject.toml` to hatchling to match the workspace convention.
   409→- **Adding `adapter-registry` to root `pyproject.toml` deps without `workspace = true`:** The root project uses `[tool.uv.sources]` to mark workspace members. Any service/lib that depends on `adapter-registry` must add it under `[tool.uv.sources]` with `{ workspace = true }`, not as a PyPI version.
   410→- **Not adding root pyproject.toml pythonpath + coverage entries:** The root `pyproject.toml` has explicit pythonpath lists in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` and `[tool.coverage.run]`. New libraries must be added there or tests won't discover them when running from root.
   411→
   412→---
   413→
   414→## Don't Hand-Roll
   415→
   416→| Problem | Don't Build | Use Instead | Why |
   417→|---------|-------------|-------------|-----|
   418→| UUID generation for adapter IDs | Custom ID scheme | `uuid.uuid4()` (stdlib) | UUIDs are the documented pattern in adapter-storage.md; stdlib, zero deps |
   419→| HTTP client for vLLM | Custom requests wrapper | `openai.AsyncOpenAI(base_url=...)` | vLLM exposes an OpenAI-compatible REST API; the openai package handles retries, streaming, connection pooling |
   420→| SQLite schema migration | Manual ALTER TABLE | Not needed for scaffold phase (deferred to implementation) | Alembic migrations are explicitly deferred to implementation milestone per REQUIREMENTS.md |
   421→| Thread-safe singleton for registry | Custom cache | `shared.lazy_cache.lazy_singleton` already exists | The lazy_singleton decorator in the shared lib handles thread-safe singleton initialization |
   422→
   423→**Key insight:** This phase is scaffolding, not implementation. Every CRUD method raises `NotImplementedError`. The value is getting the import graph correct and the type signatures locked in.
   424→
   425→---
   426→
   427→## Common Pitfalls
   428→
   429→### Pitfall 1: SQLModel `table=True` Model Import Triggers SQLAlchemy Metadata Registration
   430→
   431→**What goes wrong:** Importing a `table=True` class registers it in SQLAlchemy's global metadata. If two `table=True` models define the same table name across different imports/test runs, SQLAlchemy raises `InvalidRequestError: Table 'X' is already defined`.
   432→**Why it happens:** SQLModel's `table=True` argument calls `SQLAlchemy.MetaData.create_all`-adjacent registration at class definition time.
   433→**How to avoid:** Give `AdapterRecord` an explicit `__tablename__ = "adapter_records"` (plural, distinct from existing `entity`, `task` tables in `shared.models`). This avoids any cross-contamination.
   434→**Warning signs:** `InvalidRequestError` or `SAWarning` during test collection, especially when running across multiple libs.
   435→
   436→### Pitfall 2: `uv init --lib` Creates `uv_build` Backend, Not Hatchling
   437→
   438→**What goes wrong:** `uv init --lib` generates `build-backend = "uv_build"`. The workspace uses hatchling exclusively. If left as `uv_build`, the `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = [...]` stanza is irrelevant and hatch-specific build config doesn't apply.
   439→**Why it happens:** `uv init --lib` defaults to its own build backend as of recent versions.
   440→**How to avoid:** After `uv init --lib`, immediately edit `pyproject.toml` to replace `uv_build` with hatchling and add the `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["src/adapter_registry"]` stanza.
   441→**Warning signs:** `uv build` works but hatchling-specific behavior (like `force-include`) is silently skipped.
   442→
   443→### Pitfall 3: `openai` Not in Lockfile — Must Be Added to `inference` Dependencies
   444→
   445→**What goes wrong:** `libs/inference/pyproject.toml` does not declare `openai` as a dependency. Attempting `from openai import AsyncOpenAI` in `adapter_loader.py` will fail at import time even though `openai` might exist in a dev environment.
   446→**Why it happens:** `openai` was not needed by the existing inference codebase (which uses langchain-google-vertexai or stubs).
   447→**How to avoid:** Add `openai` to `libs/inference/pyproject.toml` dependencies and run `uv lock`. This will add openai and its deps (httpx, pydantic, etc.) to the lockfile. Since httpx and pydantic are already in the lockfile, the delta will be minimal.
   448→**Warning signs:** `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai'` when running the importability test.
   449→
   450→### Pitfall 4: Root `pyproject.toml` Consistency — Five Hardcoded Sections
   451→
   452→**What goes wrong:** The root `pyproject.toml` has five places that enumerate components explicitly: `[tool.uv.workspace] members`, `[[tool.mypy.overrides]] module`, `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath`, `[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths`, and `[tool.coverage.run] source`. Adding `adapter-registry` without updating all five causes tests to not discover the new package, mypy to flag missing stubs, and coverage to miss the new code.
   453→**Why it happens:** The root config predates the glob-based Makefile pattern; its explicit lists must be kept in sync manually.
   454→**How to avoid:** After creating `adapter-registry`, update all five sections in the root `pyproject.toml`. Use `libs/adapter-registry/src` (pythonpath) and `libs/adapter-registry` (testpaths/workspace member).
   455→**Warning signs:** `pytest` collects no tests for adapter_registry; mypy emits `Module "adapter_registry" has no attribute "AdapterRecord"`.
   456→
   457→### Pitfall 5: `model-training` Already Has `torch` as Hard Dependency
   458→
   459→**What goes wrong:** `libs/model-training/pyproject.toml` declares `torch>=2.0.0` as a runtime dependency. On a CPU-only machine without a CUDA-capable torch wheel, `uv sync` may pull a CPU-only torch (which is fine), but any code doing `import torch` in a stub will work — it just won't have GPU. The real risk is if `peft` or `bitsandbytes` are added as dependencies: those packages have platform-specific wheels and CUDA requirements that can break CPU importability.
   460→**Why it happens:** `peft` and `bitsandbytes` are GPU-required at install time on some platforms.
   461→**How to avoid:** Do NOT add `peft`, `bitsandbytes`, or `transformers` to `model-training`'s dependencies in this phase. The stubs that call `peft.LoraConfig` should use `TYPE_CHECKING` guards. The mypy `ignore_missing_imports` override for `peft.*` is already in place in the root `pyproject.toml`.
   462→**Warning signs:** `uv sync` fails with platform-specific wheel resolution errors; `uv run pytest` fails with CUDA-related import errors on CPU machines.
   463→
   464→### Pitfall 6: `SQLModel` Table Conflicts Across Test Runs
   465→
   466→**What goes wrong:** When pytest runs the full workspace test suite from root, it imports multiple SQLModel `table=True` models across different libs. If the same table name is registered twice, SQLAlchemy raises on the second registration.
   467→**Why it happens:** SQLAlchemy's global metadata is process-global; all imports in a single pytest process share it.
   468→**How to avoid:** Ensure `AdapterRecord.__tablename__` is unique (e.g., `"adapter_records"`) and does not clash with `"entity"` or `"task"` in `shared.models`.
   469→**Warning signs:** `sqlalchemy.exc.InvalidRequestError: Table 'X' is already defined for this MetaData instance` during test collection.
   470→
   471→---

   473→## Code Examples
   474→
   475→Verified patterns from official sources:
   476→
   477→### uv workspace: Add existing directory as member
   478→
   479→```toml
   480→# Source: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/
   481→# Root pyproject.toml [tool.uv.workspace]
   482→[tool.uv.workspace]
   483→members = [
   484→    "services/api-service",
   485→    "services/rune-agent",
   486→    "libs/adapter-registry",   # <- add new member here
   487→    "libs/data-pipeline",
   488→    "libs/evaluation",
   489→    "libs/events-py",
   490→    "libs/inference",
   491→    "libs/model-training",
   492→    "libs/shared",
   493→]
   494→```
   495→
   496→### uv workspace: Declare workspace dependency in another lib
   497→
   498→```toml
   499→# Source: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/dependencies/
   500→# Example: if a service depends on adapter-registry
   501→[project]
   502→dependencies = ["adapter-registry"]
   503→
   504→[tool.uv.sources]
   505→adapter-registry = { workspace = true }
   506→```

   510→```python
   511→# Source: Context7 /openai/openai-python
   512→from openai import AsyncOpenAI
   513→
   514→client = AsyncOpenAI(
   515→    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
   516→    api_key="not-needed",  # vLLM local deployments don't require a real key

   525→### SQLModel `table=True` with explicit tablename
   526→
   527→```python
   528→# Source: Context7 /websites/sqlmodel_tiangolo
   529→from typing import Optional
   530→from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel
   531→
   532→class AdapterRecord(SQLModel, table=True):
   533→    __tablename__ = "adapter_records"  # explicit to avoid conflicts
   534→
   535→    id: str = Field(primary_key=True)
   536→    task_type: str = Field(index=True)
   537→    # ...
   538→```

   540→### Importability test pattern (matching events-py style in the repo)
   541→
   542→```python
   543→# libs/adapter-registry/tests/test_importability.py
   544→from adapter_registry import (
   545→    AdapterRecord,
   546→    AdapterRegistry,
   547→    AdapterAlreadyExistsError,
   548→    AdapterNotFoundError,
   549→)
   550→import pytest
   551→
   552→
   553→def test_adapter_record_is_importable() -> None:
   554→    """AdapterRecord can be imported without GPU."""
   555→    assert AdapterRecord is not None
   556→
   557→
   558→def test_adapter_registry_stubs_raise_not_implemented() -> None:
   559→    """All stub CRUD methods raise NotImplementedError."""
   560→    registry = AdapterRegistry()
   561→    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError):
   562→        registry.list_all()
   563→```

### Key Design Decisions

- **All 3 plans in Wave 1 (parallel):** No file overlap between plans -- adapter-registry is a new lib, shared gets a new file, model-training/inference get new files. All can execute concurrently.
- **No `shared` dependency for adapter-registry:** Per research recommendation, keeping dependency graph minimal in Phase 5. Can add in Phase 6 if a service needs both.
- **No peft/bitsandbytes/transformers in deps:** model-training stubs use TYPE_CHECKING guards only. Adding GPU packages would risk breaking `uv sync` on CPU-only machines.
- **`openai` added to inference deps (not vllm):** The openai package with `base_url` is the CPU-safe, documented pattern for vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API.

   **AdapterRef** (reference to a stored LoRA adapter):
   - `adapter_id: str` — UUID of the adapter
   - `task_type: str` — task category (e.g. 'bug-fix', 'feature-impl')
   - `fitness_score: Optional[float] = None` — evolutionary fitness score

   **CodingSession** (a complete agent coding session):
   - `session_id: str` — unique session identifier
   - `task_description: str` — human-readable task description
   - `task_type: str` — task category
   - `adapter_refs: list[AdapterRef] = []` — adapters used in this session
   - `attempt_count: int = 0` — number of generate-execute-reflect cycles
   - `outcome: Optional[str] = None` — 'success' | 'exhausted' | None (in progress)

   **EvolMetrics** (evolution evaluation metrics for an adapter):
   - `adapter_id: str` — UUID of the adapter being evaluated
   - `pass_rate: float` — pass rate on benchmark tasks
   - `fitness_score: float` — overall evolutionary fitness
   - `generalization_delta: Optional[float] = None` — difference between in-distribution and OOD performance

     3→## What This Is
     4→
     5→Rune is a local-first coding agent that uses LoRA weight space as episodic memory, enabling unbounded context for Small Language Models (<10B params). Instead of stuffing tokens into context windows, Rune encodes procedural knowledge—architecture specs, execution feedback, coding conventions—directly into composable LoRA adapters via a Doc-to-LoRA hypernetwork. Each coding session produces reusable adapters that persist across sessions and compose hierarchically.
     6→
     7→## Core Value
     8→
     9→A local coding agent that learns from its own coding trajectories, building persistent parametric memory that scales independently of context window size.
    10→

    39→## Context
    40→
    41→- **Existing codebase**: Monorepo template with FastAPI backend, React/Vite frontend, LangGraph agent orchestration, SQLModel persistence, uv workspace management. Rune will be built on top of this foundation.
    42→- **Hardware target**: Dual RTX 4090 (24GB each, 48GB total VRAM) with CXL interconnect, AMD Threadripper 7960X. Ada Lovelace (sm_89) has mature CUDA/PyTorch/vLLM support. CXL provides cache-coherent memory pooling. QLoRA important for fitting models + adapters in 24GB per GPU.
    43→- **Research basis**: Architecture synthesized from multiple papers (Doc-to-LoRA, S-LoRA, QLoRA, Perceiver, HyperNetworks). No hands-on experiments yet — plan should include early feasibility validation.
    44→- **Key papers**: Sakana AI Doc-to-LoRA (arXiv:2602.15902), S-LoRA (arXiv:2311.03285), QLoRA (arXiv:2305.14314)
    45→- **Base model candidates**: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B (per spec). 24GB per GPU means QLoRA is essential; ~7B models fit comfortably with adapter headroom
    46→
    47→## Constraints
    48→
    49→- **Local-first**: Must run entirely on local hardware. No cloud API dependencies for inference.
    50→- **Hardware**: Dual RTX 4090 + CXL + Threadripper 7960X (48GB VRAM total, CXL memory pooling, high CPU core count)
    51→- **Monorepo**: Build on existing template structure (uv workspace, FastAPI, React)
    52→- **Python**: Primary implementation language, using uv for package management
    53→- **Research stage**: No working implementation exists — plan must include validation checkpoints

     1→This is an excellent paper with highly relevant insights for Rune. The **Programming by Backprop (PBB)** research directly validates and extends our core thesis about parametric episodic memory. Here are the key insights we should incorporate: [arxiv](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2506.18777)
     2→
     3→## Critical Findings from Programming by Backprop
     4→
     5→**1. Code Internalizes Algorithmic Abstractions via Backpropagation** [arxiv](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2506.18777)
     6→
     7→The paper demonstrates that LLMs trained on source code *without* input-output examples can still evaluate those programs on new inputs. This happens through standard backpropagation—the model learns to encode procedural logic directly in its weights. This is precisely what Rune does with LoRA adapters.
     8→
     9→**2. Code > Natural Language for Abstraction Learning** [arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.18777.pdf)
    10→
    11→PBB works "significantly better when programs are provided as code rather than semantically equivalent language descriptions." This validates our approach of encoding project specifications, architecture rules, and execution feedback as *structured code representations* rather than prose documentation.
    12→
    13→**3. Compositional Evaluation from Independent Training** [themoonlight](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/programming-by-backprop-llms-acquire-reusable-algorithmic-abstractions-during-code-training)
    14→
    15→Models can evaluate *compositions* of programs they were trained on independently. This directly supports our Evolution Operator's consolidation strategy—merging adapters trained on separate trajectories should enable compositional reasoning about combined functionality.
    16→
    17→**4. Robustness Across Input Distributions** [themoonlight](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/programming-by-backprop-llms-acquire-reusable-algorithmic-abstractions-during-code-training)
    18→
    19→Code-trained models via PBB show "more robust evaluation across input variations" compared to I/O-trained models. This mitigates the "embers of autoregression" problem where models overfit to demonstration distributions. Our adapter-based memory should exhibit similar robustness.
    20→
    21→**5. Chain-of-Thought Enhances Reliability** [arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.18777.pdf)
    22→
    23→While models can implicitly evaluate programs in the forward pass, explicit chain-of-thought "stepping through the program" is more reliable, especially for longer programs. This informs our System-2 reasoning loop design.
    24→
    25→## Specific Modifications for Rune
    26→
    27→I should update the documentation to incorporate these insights:
    28→
    29→### 1. **Training Data Strategy** (Phase 1.4)
    30→- Include successful execution trajectories *without* input-output pairs in hypernetwork training
    31→- Train on code representations of architectural patterns, not just prose documentation
    32→- This enables PBB-style internalization of procedural abstractions
    33→
    34→### 2. **Hypernetwork Training Objective** (Phase 4.2)
    35→- Add a PBB-inspired objective: adapter should enable program evaluation without explicit I/O context
    36→- Test: generate adapter from code, evaluate on held-out inputs without those inputs in context window
    37→
    38→### 3. **Chain-of-Thought Integration** (Phase 2.3)
    39→- System-2 reasoning should include explicit step-through execution traces
    40→- These traces become training signal for hypernetwork
    41→- Validates Cook et al.'s finding that CoT improves reliability
    42→
    43→### 4. **Compositional Memory Validation** (Phase 3.2)
    44→- Test that merged adapters enable evaluation of composite programs
    45→- Example: merge "authentication" + "database access" adapters → can execute combined auth+DB logic
    46→- Direct validation of PBB's compositional generalization findings
    47→
    48→### 5. **Code-First Encoding** (Throughout)
    49→- Emphasize that project specifications, architectural constraints, and conventions should be encoded as *executable code examples* or *code-like structured representations*
    50→- Not prose documentation—actual code that demonstrates the abstraction
    51→
    52→
